notes.title: No Man's Land remade
notes.content:
For a long time, I have been trying to find solutions on how to improve No Man's Land, as it is the game's biggest flaw due to how driven people get to try to explore it even when warned against doing so. There was also the minimap that didn't want to function correctly in it no matter what.

Ultimately the solution was to remake the map but smaller. Overall it's [b]6.5x[/b] smaller.  (100x100 vs the original 255x255). It's the same size as each of the hub areas for the nations. This will make it much easier to navigate, with the minimap working fully and it's harder to get fully lost without any hope for finding anything.

The original side quests and everything has been carried over and functions like intended. If you are in a current save in the original No Man's Land, your save won't be corrupted, leaving the area and going back will bring you to the new version. It won't impact any side quests in your save files either, as it will be a seamless transition.

I apologize it took this long, I was trying to find other solutions, but this ended up being the best fix overall.

notes.title: New starting item and some fixes
notes.content:
The biggest thing in this update is the new starting item. [b]The Eye of Wonder.[/b] This item allows teleportation with any class, but at the cost of all of your money. You can choose to use it to skip the tutorial if you wish, but doing so before choosing a nation will actively lock you out of certain nation exclusive content. 

[b]But why add this?[/b]

Mostly since No Man's Land is a big hindrance to people's enjoyment with how it is, so a way for fast travel that is rare for it to work for the lore but allows more freedom for players. There is a class with fast travel already, but most players might not want to pick that for the ability to fast travel, since that is only 1 out of 15 classes. So for now, adding this item is the best solution. The Fowler class is still unique on it's own with it's stats, default of one shield before stun, and it's flying attacks.

notes.title: Wishlist Throne Requiem today!
notes.content:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3174830/Throne_Requiem/

Note: This is made in a new engine compared to Umbra Fields with many systems from it redone and expanded with more depth, but with a focus on one main area and dungeons connected to it.

Embark on a dark, brutal quest in this first-person, party-based dungeon crawler. Choose from 42 classes to form your 6-member team and conquer the Dark Tower. Every decision matters in this medieval world where insanity and death are commonplace. Will you survive?



Before everything was normal. Then the sun began blackened, the skies full of blood, and the light became the most traded resource. The beasts entered the world, kingdoms fell and new villages prospered. Humanity banded together to the Gate of the Abyss, sending parties to explore and to kill whatever Dark God created the Abyss.

Those who enter will gain broken bones, infections, and will bleed to death, unless they are prepared.



The Town is a nameless place where those who go into the Abyss rest in. It has everything a traveler would need. Stores, a church, a prison, a town hall, and more. Get quests to do things in the town, or the help out the people, they give many gifts and new teachings to survive. Go to stores to buy and sell, or to loot and slaughter whoever runs them. Ignore the cries from the prison, or help them with revenge. The stores run on a stock market simulation in the background, impacting if they stay around or not. 

You are going to need lots of food, steel, and courage to survive. Make sure to always be strong, always be sane, and to eat before your food rots. 

Outside of the town, the beasts may make your party go insane. Maintaining the sanity level for each party member is key to survival. Set up Campfires for everybody to speak their mind, search for goods, and more depending on how they are. If not, then when they go insane they will leave the party as they shout the unknown.

How much you can purchase or get loans depends on your Credit Score with the people, and how much debt you get yourself into. Buy things and you will look better for loans. Loans gives money but debt that quickly compounds. If you get into too much debt, a debt collector will come to collect a soul.



Your 6 crew members are fragile with their mounds of flesh. They begin with something unique to each one.

Kestrel - They are the Leader. The speeches they give can give great passion to the party during battle, or great despair.
Graham - A strong sense of morals, they may be a strong member.
Ceolumnd - They want to seek out the group more than themselves, allowing and begging the beasts to attack them instead of the others.
Chad - A famous person outside of the Abyss. This has lead them to develop a strong sense of pride.
Deorwine - A sickly person. They have a deadly infection that is slowly eating their insides out. They have a medication that makes them very sick, but gives them more time to survive. Anything without side effects is expensive, but maybe the town offers many different ways to remove the infection.
Oswald - Someone who has had a dark past, and had to learn to syphon energy from others at a young age. This is very effective in battle.

Yet, one of them maybe be a traitor. This is something randomized at the start of the game if someone has a darker shimmer of a thought of betrayal. Only one may be a betrayer. Be warned, you may not be able to fully trust your party members in the end. 



There are 42 classes to choose from. Your party composition will impact how easy or hard it is to survive. Be warned, not every class are equal in the eyes of the people.

Knight - A common warrior, those who use the blade to seek adventure. 
Archer - One great with a bow who used to serve  the guard to a great wall.
Mage - Someone who knows magic, but isn't gifted in a single area of it/
Rogue - A scout who uses more traditional weapons for villages instead of nobles, and thus isn't as good as finding out secrets.
Doctor - One who knows how to cure broken bones and infections quickly. 
Bard - One through song and dance gives life to the party.
Druid - A man of the Earth who speaks to the earthy beasts.
Monk - A holy man who wants to seek ascendance through prayer.
Alchemist - A potion creator who used to make a living selling potions. They can create unknown potions or the strongest potions man has ever seen.

Berserker - A warrior who can go berserk, an unstable but stronger state during battle.
Sorcerer - Weak physically, as they gave up all of their years for the craft of magics.
Artificer - They can fuse holy weapons and create weapons only they may use. 
Enchanter - Heavily focused on buffing and debuffing, they may also go to the Town under the fountain to give a stronger buff to the party.
Assassin - A weaker warrior who lives in the shadows for stronger attacks.
Jester - A King's joker, who knows how to buff the party, and maybe tell a joke.
Mystic - Someone who knows how to speak to roaming spirits and to use them against beasts.
Templar - A holy knight of the crusade, who goes for the Pope to slave the Darkness. 
Shapeshifter - A formless being that can transform into different things to change how they are in combat.

Summoner - One who summons beasts in battle to take their place.
Psionic - One who can read minds and use it against them in combat.
Runemaster - One who has studied and mastered the runes the beasts use. They require items for major attacks.
Witch - A swamp hag who bewitches her opponents. 
Seer - Someone who can see the future, but isn't against lying if it benefits them.
Geomancer - A man of the Earth, they know and can deal with boulders.
Duelist - Someone skilled with a blade, using their passion to fuel them.
Farmer - A man who knows how to grow food. In the Tower, they are best with collecting Mushrooms.
Cook - Someone who knows how to cook. They can cook at campfires or special places which gives great joy and extra bonuses. Don't let any cooked food rot.

Juggernaut - One covered in armor head to toe. Slow but strong.
Pyromancer - A man of the limited flame. They can set up camp fires for free, and use fire magic.
Frost Mage - A man of the frost. They can freeze anything.
Stormcaller - A man of the storms. They can call lighting from any skies.
Puppet - A soul trapped in a puppet's body, it is weak, yet it is infused with magic.
Demonologist - A man who has drank enough blood to transform to speak to demons. They have many gifts, but they all require sacrifice. Christians don't like them.
Scout - A man who knows how to watch for threats, and to find things near a campfire. Uses a trusty gun to survive.
Prisoner - A man of Sin. They may steal from the party, but may get bonuses when having low Karma.
Karma Sage - They are men of the one true God. Their strength is based around strong Karma. Pagans dislike them, and they are banned from Pagan Churches.

Merchant - Merchants are men of the coin and of debt. They can accept debt for bonuses, and abuse debt for their own gain. Gamblers, they may also enter the Stock market in the town to buy stocks for the stores.
Noble - They gain strength on how well known they are and are worshipped by the people.
Monkey - Highly aggressive pets trained to fight the beasts. They are known to go Feral and attack friend and foe.
Leper - Very sick, worse at campfires to support everyone, can inflict infections onto enemies.
Villager - Nothing special. The lesser known the party is, the stronger a special attack they have is.
Beggar - Poor, they know how to beg, but not everybody will answer in kind.



Battles are fierce. The Beasts are strong and mighty. They will break your bones, make you bleed, and infect you. Sometimes bigger enemies can be found that will give a challenge. But they will all eat away at the mind, some giving trauma to those who fight them.

Major battles will have special choice based attacks, where it can reshape the battle depending on a good or bad choice. A bad one may leading to an unrecoverable death.




The Town may have a Pagan or a Christian Church when you arrive. They have many offerings, mostly after some donations. Some quests and some rewards to those who require any Holy Orbs. But alas, there may be more. The Beasts have their own statues in the main dungeon, with their own gods. Renounce humanity's Gods and give worship, and they may answer when you pray. Or destroy the false Gods. Yet, don't believe you will be allowed back in the Church once you renounce your faith. It is all up to you who you worship and call God.



All choices made can be good or bad for humanity. You may become a party that serves the best of man, or only themselves. This will impact how you are viewed by the people, and what may impact your choices in the end...



With your party formed, it will take lots of blood and sweat to survive and to get to the end. Can you survive? Can you fight the Dark God and overthrow the endless night?

notes.title: Tips and Tricks for the Umbra Fields for new players
notes.content:
Before playing Umbra Fields, have some small quick tips and tricks.

[b]Class Related tips: [/b]

Warrior: Very well balanced. Made to do anything with a focus on physical attacks. Put your bonus points into physical attack and magical defense. Recommend for new players.

Doctor: Doctors are very strong, as they can quickly heal injuries and is immune to the Plague. More of a support, they reply on other party members more. Recommend for new players.

Thief: Is very fast and can steal money and items from enemies and shopkeepers. Most shopkeepers will not sell to Thieves, and their wanted level will always be higher than most. Focus on agility with bonus points.

Hunter: Hunters are focused on their bows and being very aggressive and offensive when possible along with having traps to cause debuffs to enemies in battle. Physical attacks should be buffed with bonus points. Recommend for new players.

Rune Master: Rune masters are all about setting up stronger attacks with runes. Some unique locations only they can discover. Requires more strategy than most other classes due to this reason.

Summoner: They can summon creatures to protect themselves if they have the materials and find a summoning circle. Mostly a support, they can create some of the most powerful minions if they travel and explore enough. Requires lots of strategy until a strong minion is created.

Ice Spearmen: Fishermen who fish whenever they can find any remaining, clean water. Fish can be sold or eaten for buffs and healing. They are very self sufficient, and spending some time fishing whenever possible is recommended. 

Investigator: A detective that can use guns, talk to enemies when able, and can take on cases for others. If you are cunning enough, some will join you by speech alone. Some will also take the pause to attack instead. Requires more strategy due to all of the new options available. 

Priest: The Gods need priests to spread their holy words, teaching them holy magic. Priests are made to travel the land to find a god or gods to worship, and in return strong holy magic is learned which gives a very strong buff. Recommend for new players.

Brute: A Warrior that has no honor, fierce in the wild, yet cannot live among civilization. Very aggressive in their main attacks and less defense than the Warrior. They require bonus points being put into defense, especially magic defense.

Storm Evoker: The Forbidden one was one of these, a being that can control the storms. The outcasts worship Evokers, others fear them. Mostly uses physical attacks and lighting attacks, they can be a major force to anything in their way.

Fowler: Flying beasts that can travel to any place they please, but are hunted. A Fowler can quickly travel to place to place to experience many things easily and quickly. They have the weakest defense and can easily be stunned. Defense in Magic and Physical is required with bonus points, and getting new armor and accessories for more break shields is needed. 

Fire Elemental: Due to the Great War, The Flame has made all Fire Elemental to be worshiped and adored. Yet not all feel the same way. The Flame is the best nation to start at due to all of the bonuses. Talking to other fire elementals gives free healing too. Very aggressive, magic attack should be focused with bonus points. Recommend for new players.

The Slime: A mistake not meant to live. An experiment to remove all bones so you can no longer be injured and stronger in battle, it comes with a downside. Your body is made out of a liquid mush that is weak to everything. Only those who wish for pain choose the slime. The slime can quickly be killed due to it's weaknesses, so it must spend the most time to prepare before bigger battles before fighting to make sure it won't easily be killed by getting new armor and protection. This is mostly something to be a hardmode for anybody who wishes for a harder experience.

The Blameless: One who is random with their speech, and their spells. They cannot be blamed for their actions, as every time they open their mouths, it is unknown what will come out. Beasts of the Umbra Fields attack them last, knowing their randomness can be beneficial. Getting party members will drastically improve your chances of survival, and it's random main spell can be beneficial or harmful at random, so putting too much faith in it can be devastating. 


[b]Nation Related tips: [/b]

The Flame: Highly recommend playing as a fire elemental for choosing this nation as a starting nation due to the benefits. If your class isn't one, then it won't be as easy of a time.

The Land of the Sea: Islands can have some strong treasure, but are usually protected. The zombies that protect them are very easy to kill, outside the main Shamans. 

The Gaea Forrest: Since it has the most infrastructure that remains, it is the easiest to travel in and explore. Very non-linear, so you can do anything in any order to gain any skills in any order. Going to the school gives free stat points, while the fortune teller's abilities are very strong. 

Angelic Constabulary: The Guardian party member can be gotten here if starting in this nation, doing side quests can increase it's potential. Taking to the scientist after each main quest for the nation can give some free skills as well.

The Prison: Has some strong party members to recruit, and the prison food is strong. A doctor is immune to the prison food's illnesses.

Lich Fields: Lots to explore and find, with very strong weapons for daggers and staff hidden away. Thieves and Fowlers can get some of their strongest weapons here. 

Pig Nation: The luck blast is one of the strongest attacks that can be gotten with luck. The Pig Bonds are great for storing money along with the Bank so it doesn't get stolen in battle. The Arena is a great place to get EXP and money.

No Man's Land: If the player isn't an outcast or of certain classes, then it's best not to stay too long.

[b]General tips: [/b]

In the first area, it is highly recommended to do all of the side quests for their specific skills.

Side quests are the best place to gain more strength and skills for battle. Do them when you can.

If you do get the Chocolate Truffle and deliver it into No Man's Land, there is a major reward that can drastically help with survival.

Exploring is one of the best things you can do once you believe you have everything from the nation you are in. Beware of No Man's Land, it doesn't have a lot for those who don't live there outside hungry beasts.

Injuries and aliments are key to success. Physical attacks can cause injuries quickly, and Magic attacks can cause an aliment based on the element being used. Some enemies get stronger when injured. Most get weaker. When Injured, concussions are the ones that last the shortest in battle, but has the biggest impact. A single injury or aliment can turn the tide of battle instantly, and some attacks cause them more than others. Getting armor to resist them would be highly beneficial.

Boost Points are very strong for boosting abilities and using stronger ones locked behind them. Save them for bigger attacks or to boost abilities when closer to the max amount of them during battle.

Magic stones are very expensive but very strong in battle. Boost Points can be used with them in battle to quickly kill enemies. You should save them for minibosses and bosses you are stuck on.

If fighting against a Thief, killing them gives lots of gold, but every turn is another opportunity for them to steal. Running away from a Thief might be beneficial if you cannot kill it fast enough.

There are some hidden, secret bosses and routes. They are much harder than the stuff in the normal game. Only attempt them if you have a full party and are strong enough.

I recommend playing on normal first, since the other difficulties mostly add new abilities for enemies that drastically changes how battles are thought of and how they are fought. Normal allows for more easier experimentation with the mechanics for a better understanding, while the harder difficulties will be very punishing for letting your guard down. They are very different beasts than the normal difficulty. 

There are over 14 main endings in the game. You will not be able to experience everything in one playthrough, it's impossible to. In fact, you would have to do many different playthroughs to experience everything. Do what you can with your choices, own up to them, and have fun.

notes.title: Wishlist Umbra Fields today!
notes.content:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2652040/Umbra_Fields/

No matter what you choose, and what you do, you will have an impact upon the world. Do you wish to be a criminal, or a savior? That is up to you.

Choose between 13 distinct classes:

Warrior: A well balanced with a focus on strength. Made to do any quests.

Doctor: Healers that can heal the sickness across each nation, yet are weak on their own.

Thief: Shopkeepers never sell to them, with their moves constantly under watch. Going to The Prison, is the least of the thief's worries.

Hunter: They live for the hunt and the slaughter. They can be found to get good pay from hunting rare beasts.

Rune Master: The old and intelligent beings that can read cosmic words.

Summoner: They can summon creatures to protect themselves. Hated by most, they are targeted for creating abominations upon the world.

Ice Spearmen: Fishermen who fish whenever they can find any remaining, clean water.

Investigator: A detective that can use guns, talk to enemies when able, and can take on cases for others. If you are cunning enough, some will join you by speech alone.

Priest: The Gods need priests to spread their holy words, teaching them holy magic. 

Brute: A Warrior that has no honor, fierce in the wild, yet cannot live among civilization.

Storm Evoker: The Forbidden one was one of these, a being that can control the storms. The outcasts worship Evokers, others fear them.

Fowler: Flying beasts that can travel to any place they please, but are hunted.

Fire Elemental: Due to the Great War, The Flame has made all Fire Elemental to be worshiped and adored. Yet not all feel the same way.



Whatever you become, you shall be the prey of others from man to beast. Master who you are and what you will become to manage your stamina, hit weaknesses, stun enemies, and kill to survive. Do quests to get stronger, to learn more to use more magics and skills.

Choose your nation:

The Flame: A land of The Flame, an active volcano where Fire Elementals are born.

The Land of the Sea: A land once known for it's Ice, it has become melted to be a grand Sea.

The Grand Tree: The last of nature, all connected to the Mother Tree.

Angelic Constabulary: A land for the last of the an holy order that wants to maintain law.

The Prison: Those who break the law are sent to the Prison to rot, while it's controlled by a Mafia.

Lich Fields: Sky islands full of the rot and sickness where Wizards and Summoners roam free.

Pig Nation: A nation isolated from the rest after The Great War, run by the pigs who have no God.

No Man's Land: The only thing that connects the nations together, only the outcasts live here and the beasts roam free.
